ψάμμη.definition: rarer form of Hdt.4.181 , who elsewh. always has the common form: Dor. A.Pr.573 , Ar.Lys.1261

ψάμμητον.definition: a kind of cake, Harp. s.v

ψάμμος.definition: but in Archim.Aren.1.1, al., always; metallic ore used by alchemists, in pl., Olymp.Alch.p.106B., Zos.Alch.p.239 B

ψαρός.definition: like a starling, i. e. speckled, dappled, a dapple-grey horse, Ar.Nu.1225, LXXZa.1.8; Arist.HA632b19 distinguishes it fr. which implies that the spots are more distinctly marked:—Comp. Ael.NA12.28, Aët.11.11

ψευδάριον.definition: fallacy, in pl. title of work by Euclid, Procl.in Euc.p.70F., cf. p.59 F

ψῆξις.definition: rubbing down, currying, of horses, X.Eq.5.3,10

ψῆφος.definition: Dor. Aeol. gen. pl; precious stone, gem, Philostr.VA3.27; esp. worn in a ring, Luc.DMeretr.9

ψοΐτης.definition: lumbar portion of the spinal cord, Gal.8.328

ψόρος.definition: an unknown fish, Numen. ap. Ath.7.313e; also Speus. ibid

ψύγμα.definition: a means of cooling, anything that; a cooling lotion, Hp.Morb.2.16 ; a cooling medicine, Id.Aff.11

ψύθος.definition: poet. collat. form for lie, untruth, A.Ag.478 , 999 , 1089 :—in Call.Fr.184, is a Subst. in appos. with

ψύλλα.definition: a venomous spider, perhaps Lathrodectes or malmignatte, Arist.HA622b31

ψῦξις.definition: a cooling, chilling; a being or becoming cold, ib.16; Pl.Ti.85d: pl., opp. Id.Tht.156b; opp. Lg.897a, Arist.GA777b27

ψῦχος.definition: cold, Emp.65.2; opp; once in Hom., coolness, Od.10.555: metaph., A.Ag.971

ψώα.definition: rottenness, putrid stench, A.R.Fr.5: but Hdn.Epim.155

ψωλή.definition: Dor. prop. fem. of membrum virile praeputio retracto, Ar.Lys.143, Av.560 , Supp.Epigr.3.596

ψαίρω.definition: only pres., and not in Att. Prose; trans., graze, brush lightly, touch gently, . . is ready to skim the path of ether, A.Pr.396; rub, scrape gently in washing, Eun.VSp.486B

ψαίω.definition: = , rub away, grind down, in aor. 1 Med., Thphr. ap.Porph.Abst.2.6:—aor. Pass., ibid

ψακάζω.definition: later :—rain in small drops, drizzle, drip, Ar.Nu.580: impers., it drizzles, let it rain loaves, Nicoph.13:—Med., . . they like n a short-sighted person to a spluttering lamp, prob. in Arist.Rh.1413a4 :—Pass., moisten…

ψάλιον.definition: part of the bridle, curb-chain; generally, chain, bond, A.Pr.54 : metaph., Id.Ch.962

ψάλμα.definition: tune played on a stringed instrument, AP11.34 , Max.Tyr.37.4

ψαλμός.definition: twitching or twanging with the fingers; mostly of musical strings, Telest.5, cf. Diog.Trag.1.9, Aret.CA1.1

ψαμμιαῖος.definition: of the size of a grain of sand, Olymp.in Phd.p.31 N

ψαμμουργία.definition: and art of extracting gold from sand, Zos.Alch.p.241 B

ψαύω.definition: touch lightly. a way of feeling the pulse, opp. Gal.8.808: metaph., touch upon a subject, notice it slightly, Plb.1.13.8:—Med., c. acc. rei, touch lightly upon a subject, Gal.18.331

ψάω.definition: but always contracted], S.Tr.678, inf; intr., crumble away, vanish, disappear, S.Tr.678

ψελιόω.definition: twine, wreathe, AP7.234; Med., put on an armlet, subject of statue by Praxiteles, Plin.HN34.70

ψελλίζω.definition: falter in speech, speak; metaph., of a boy soldier, Philostr.Her.19.2

ψέλλισμα.definition: inarticulate speech, of a child's attempts at talking, Him.Or.23.21; of a nurse's 'baby-talk', Sor.1.109

ψελλιστής.definition: stammerer, Gloss; of horses who injure their hoofs in the stable, Hippiatr.10

ψευδογράφος.definition: a drawer of false diagrams; writer of falsehoods, Thom.Mag.p.224 R.: = falsarius, Gloss

ψευδοφαής.definition: shining with false, i.e. borrowed, light, of the moon, D.L.2.1

ψεύδω.definition: S.Ant.389, etc.: fut. Id.OC628; c. gen., cheat, balk, disappoint one of a thing, E.Hec.1031; A.Pers.472; Ar.Th.870; . . . . X.Cyr.1.5.13; E.Fr.650:—Pass., to be cheated balked, disappointed, of a thing, Hdt.1.141, 5.4…

ψηλαφάω.definition: mostly used in pres.: fut. LXXZa.9.13; c. acc. rei, feel about for, grope or search after, Ar.Pax691; . . Act.Ap.17.27

ψηνίζω.definition: to Psenize, alluding to the a Comedy by Magnes so called, Ar.Eq.523

ψηφίζω.definition: fut. Att. Aeschin.2.84: aor; i.e. if you add up the numerical values of the letters in the word Theol.Ar.64

ψηφίον.definition: Dim. of small pebble, gravel, Aq.Am.9.9; pellet, Orib.Fr.35

ψηφίς.definition: pebble for reckoning, AP11.365; tessellated work, Chor.p.86B

ψηφόω.definition: adorn with gems, Lyd.Mag.1.4, cf; work in mosaic, Supp.Epigr.7.993 ; adorn with mosaics

ψήχω.definition: Ar.Fr.42, etc.: fut. X.Eq.4.4:—Pass., aor; scratch, dub. in Jul.Caes.310a

ψιθύρισμα.definition: any low whispering noise, as of trees rustling, Theoc.1.1

ψιλοποιέω.definition: write with a smooth breathing, Theodoretus in cod. Barocc. 68

ψιλόω.definition: strip bare, mostly of hair; c. gen., strip bare of, Hp.Art.1:—Pass., Id.Aph.5.22, cf. Art.69, Arist.HA519b5

ψίλωμα.definition: bone laid bare of flesh, Hp.Art.69, cf. Epid.3.4

ψίλωσις.definition: stripping bare of flesh; Gramm., writing or pronouncing with the spiritus lenis, or an unaspirated consonant, Eust.515.37

ψιλωτής.definition: one who writes or pronounces with the spiritus lenis, or litterae tenues, Tz.H.11.52

ψιμυθιστής.definition: one who paints with white lead or cosmetics, Gloss

ψιχίον.definition: Dim. of crumb, Ev. Matt.15.27; of stomachic residue after emesis, Archig. ap. Orib.8.23.5

ψοφέω.definition: pf. Men.Sam.324, etc.:—sound, make a; esp. of an empty noise, S.Fr.61; Alex.25.9; Call.Aet.Oxy.2079.19

ψυκτήρ.definition: cool shady places for recreation, Nic.Thyat. ap. Ath.11.503c

ψυχάζω.definition: refresh oneself in the shade, Alciphr.3.12, Ael.NA5.21, Procop.Gaz.p.175B

ψυχαῖος.definition: of the soul, Orac. Chald. ap. Lyd.Mens.1.11; Simp.in Ph.780.14

ψυχαστής.definition: one who cools himself in the shade: a play of Strattis

ψυχή.definition: life, Il.5.296, etc; metaph. of things dear as life, . . . Hes.Op.686; E.Andr.419; Timocl.35; so as an endearing name, Hld.1.8, al.; Juv.6.195; Mart.10.68

ψυχήϊος.definition: having a alive, living, Pythag. ap. Luc.Vit.Auct.6

ψυχογονία.definition: the generation of the soul, Plu.2.415e, al., Herm.in Phdr.p.128A

ψυχομαχέω.definition: fight to the last gasp, fight; suffer anguish, Lyr.Alex.Adesp.4.21

ψυχόω.definition: give soul to, APl.4.159; give a psychical character to physical sensations, Id.4.4.28

ψυχραίνω.definition: make cool or cold, cool, in Pass., Plu.Fr.inc.149, Alex.Trall.1.14, Procl.in Prm.p.571 S.: metaph., Id.Par.Ptol.270

ψυχρία.definition: chilliness; metaph. of rhetoric, frigidity, Chrysipp.Stoic.3.50, cf. Plu.Alex.3

ψυχρότης.definition: coldness, cold, opp; metaph. of persons, want of feeling, bad taste, D.18.256: sluggishness, Plu.Fab.17

ψύχω.definition: Hdt.3.104, etc.: fut. Alex.25.10; make cool or cold , Hdt.3.104, cf. Hp.VM16 ; opp. Pl.Phdr.268b; Heraclit.126; Diph.56, cf. Isoc.15.287:—Pass., grow cool or cold, Hdt.4.181, Ar.Nu.151, Pl.Phd.71b, Arist.Pr.931a1; . .…

ψωμίζω.definition: fut. Att. LXXNu.11.4:—feed by putting; give food by hand, Arist.HA592a30; bestow for food, 1 Ep.Cor.13.3

ψώρα.definition: Ion. itch, mange, scurvy, of; metaph., Gal.8.148

ψωριάω.definition: to have the itch, scab, or mange, Hp.Aph.4.77; of trees, to be scabby, cankered, esp. of the fig, Thphr.CP5.9.10, HP4.14.3, etc.; of ib.8.10.1
